title: Rust: Arrays and Slices
description: Create and use fixed-size arrays and slices in Rust.

steps.title: Create an Array
steps.description: Create an array `numbers: [i32; 5] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` and print all elements using `{:?}`.
hints: Use `println!("{:?}", numbers);` to debug-print the array.

steps.title: Access Elements
steps.description: Access and print the first (`[0]`), third (`[2]`), and last (`[len-1]`) elements of `[10, 20, 30, 40, 50]`.
hints: Use `arr.len()` to get the length, then `arr[arr.len() - 1]` for the last.

steps.title: Create with Default Value
steps.description: Create an array of 10 zeros using `[0; 10]` syntax and modify the first element to `42`. Print the array.
hints: The array must be `mut` to modify elements.

verification.failureMessage: Create [0; 10], change first to 42, and print.

steps.title: Array Slice
steps.description: Create an array `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` and print a slice of the first 3 elements using `&arr[0..3]`.
hints: `let slice = &arr[0..3];` creates a reference to elements 0, 1, 2.
Slices are views into arrays (not copies).

verification.failureMessage: Print the slice of the first 3 elements.

steps.title: Mutable Slice
steps.description: Create a mutable array `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` and modify the middle 3 elements through a mutable slice `&mut arr[1..4]`. Print the modified array.
hints: `let slice = &mut arr[1..4];` creates a mutable slice.
`slice[0] = 10;` changes element at index 1 of the original array.
The original array is modified through the slice.

verification.failureMessage: Modify elements through a mutable slice and print the array.
